content: Configurable-safety-control failure modes documented across ecosystems: (1) silent acceptance of an invalid enum value — JUnit was reported silently accepting invalid values for a severity config parameter so users believed they had configured a control they had not; (2) parsers that silently return an empty/default result on a shape they do not recognise (kiota flags-enum CSV) — a decode failure presenting as 'nothing configured'; (3) protobuf's model distinguishes open vs closed enums, with unknown values preserved in an unknown-field set rather than discarded, so an unrecognised value is never silently normalised away. The consensus prescription is: never map an unrecognised value onto the permissive branch; either reject loudly at parse time or fall back to the STRICTEST defined variant while preserving and reporting the raw unknown value.
